ad74e2aa-ebf9-417d-922a-c4108e9398d5.data: Mitosis has five phases: Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.
ad74e2aa-ebf9-417d-922a-c4108e9398d5.text_lemmatized: Mitosis has five phases: Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.

a128b8e3-6302-489b-85ee-7b1ffcad8570.text_lemmatized: During Interphase, the DNA in the cell is copied in preparation for cell division, resulting in two identical complete sets of chromosomes.

95e4c97a-d9a9-4a42-82b7-653a296ab60d.data: In Prophase, chromosomes condense into X-shaped structures that can be easily seen under a microscope, and the membrane around the nucleus dissolves away releasing the chromosomes.

5329ebbe-1e3c-4566-9f1f-421658c3c952.data: During Metaphase, the chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center of the cell, and the mitotic spindle fibers attach to each of the sister chromatids.
5329ebbe-1e3c-4566-9f1f-421658c3c952.text_lemmatized: During Metaphase, the chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center of the cell, and the mitotic spindle fibers attach to each of the sister chromatids.

68cb0bd3-afe8-44f4-93b0-03f5ddeb7fa9.data: In Anaphase, the sister chromatids are pulled apart by the mitotic spindle, which pulls one chromatid to one pole and the other chromatid to the opposite pole.
68cb0bd3-afe8-44f4-93b0-03f5ddeb7fa9.text_lemmatized: In Anaphase, the sister chromatids are pulled apart by the mitotic spindle, which pulls one chromatid to one pole and the other chromatid to the opposite pole.

f1d540b0-2bf0-41ec-895e-f21225dfa95b.data: In Telophase, a full set of chromosomes gather together at each pole of the cell, and a membrane forms around each set of chromosomes to create two new nuclei.
f1d540b0-2bf0-41ec-895e-f21225dfa95b.text_lemmatized: In Telophase, a full set of chromosomes gather together at each pole of the cell, and a membrane forms around each set of chromosomes to create two new nuclei.
